newsitem.title: FRANCE: S.Korean Daewoo takes over Algiers hotel.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Daewoo takes over Algiers hotel.

text.p: Algiers' five-star Hilton hotel, which was closed for three years, reopened its doors after South Korean Daewoo took over its management from the state-owned SAFEX company, a spokesman said on Friday.
The eight-storey hotel was also renamed Hotel International d'Alger, a management spokesman said.
"The state-owned Societe Algerienne des Foires et Expositions (SAFEX), which was the sole manager and owner, ceded its majority stakes in the hotel to Daewoo firm," he said.
But he declined to give details on the transaction.
The hotel has 340 rooms, 40 suites, a swimming pool and a golf course, he said.
The official inauguration of the hotel is expected after the country's legislative elections scheduled for June 5, 1997, he added.
Daewoo, which is expanding its business activity in North Africa, purchased Morocco's five-star Hyatt Regency hotel for $28.7 million last year.
